notices.short_title: Brooklyn Bridge Park Pier 1 Pavilion Stair Replacement
notices.description: Brooklyn Bridge Park (the Park) is an eighty-five (85) acre waterfront park in Brooklyn, NY. The Pier 1 Pavilion (20 Furman Street) is the newest addition to the Park and has three (3) sets of stairs that require remediation due to inconsistent stair tread & riser dimensions. The Park is seeking proposals for a general contractor to remove and chip out all existing concrete to expose the rebar, verify the condition of the rebar and replace if needed, create formwork to pour new concrete, and verify that the newly poured stairs comply with the requirements of BC 1011.5.4.
notices.plain: Brooklyn Bridge Park is seeking proposals from general contractors, due Oct. 5, 2026, to replace three sets of stairs at the Pier 1 Pavilion at 20 Furman Street because their tread and riser dimensions are inconsistent.

notices.short_title: NOTICE OF AWARD TO STATEN ISLAND BAGEL CAFE, INC. TO PROVIDE FOR THE OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF THE CAFETERIA AT THE NEW YORK CITY POLICE DEPARTMENT POLICE ACADEMY
notices.description: The New York City Police Department has awarded a concession agreement to Staten Island Bagel Café, Inc. (Concessionaire), whose address is 3579 Victory Blvd, Staten Island, New York 10314, to provide for the operation and maintenance of the cafeteria at the New York City Police Departments Police Academy, located at 130-30 28th Avenue, College Point, New York 11354, in the borough of Queens. This concession contract was solicited through a Competitive Sealed Proposals method, pursuant to Section 1-13 of the Concession Rules of the City of New York. notices.short_title: Develop, Deploy, Support and Maintain Existing and Future Citywide Transit Signal Priority (TSP)
notices.description: The New York City Department of Transportation (the Agency) seeks a qualified vendor to develop, deploy, support, and maintain existing and future Transit Signal Priority (TSP) corridors. The Agency has successfully deployed a centralized Transit Signal Priority (TSP) System within the Citys five boroughs. Central TSP leverages the existing ITS infrastructure, including a new Traffic Safety Network (TSN), centralized Traffic Control Systems, and on-board bus equipment to lower costs and to facilitate rapid implementation. This minimized the hardware and software required to make the TSP System operational. Existing and future bus corridors on the TSP System span approximately 200 miles and include about 3,500 signalized traffic intersections. Additionally, more corridors are planned/deployed over the next few years. This Request for Proposals (RFP)/RFx is released through PASSPort, New York Citys online procurement portal. Responses to this RFP/RFx must be submitted via PASSPort. To access the RFP/RFx, vendors should visit the PASSPort Public Portal. To reach the Public Portal, visit the following site: https://www.nyc.gov/site/mocs/passport/about-passport.page then click on the…
notices.plain: The New York City Department of Transportation is seeking a vendor, chosen through competing proposals, to develop, deploy, support and maintain its Transit Signal Priority system covering about 200 miles of bus corridors and 3,500 signalized intersections, with responses due Oct. 19, 2026.

notable.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Asian Americans for Equality Inc. a $347,648 contract, chosen through negotiation with a limited group of vendors, to provide services helping low-income immigrant families navigate systems such as education, health care and housing.

notable.short_title: Early Adolescent Skills for Emotions
notable.description: EASE enables a task-sharing model of mental health support, which engages people without a formal background in mental health to develop the necessary skills to support members of their own community experiencing emotional distress.
notable.plain: The Department of Youth and Community Development renewed its contract with The New School for $300,000 to run the Early Adolescent Skills for Emotions program, which trains people without formal mental health backgrounds to support community members experiencing emotional distress.

notable.short_title: NOTICE OF AWARD TO STATEN ISLAND BAGEL CAFE, INC. TO PROVIDE FOR THE OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE OF THE CAFETERIA AT THE NEW YORK CITY POLICE DEPARTMENT POLICE ACADEMY
notable.description: The New York City Police Department has awarded a concession agreement to Staten Island Bagel Café, Inc. (Concessionaire), whose address is 3579 Victory Blvd, Staten Island, New York 10314, to provide for the operation and maintenance of the cafeteria at the New York City Police Departments Police Academy, located at 130-30 28th Avenue, College Point, New York 11354, in the borough of Queens. This concession contract was solicited through a Competitive Sealed Proposals method, pursuant to Section 1-13 of the Concession Rules of the City of New York. The concessionaire shall pay to the City a monthly concession fee of 6% of gross receipts. Gross receipts shall mean all revenue derived from the sale of food, beverages, merchandise, catering services, and vending operations. The term of the Concession is four (4) years, from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2030, with two (2) renewal options, each for a period of three (3) years.
notable.plain: The New York City Police Department awarded Staten Island Bagel Café, Inc. a four-year concession, running from July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2030, to operate and maintain the cafeteria at its Police Academy in College Point, Queens, paying the city 6% of gross receipts.

watching.short_title: NYC BOARD OF HEALTH MEETING ANNOUNCEMENT
watching.description: NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Board of Health will hold a meeting on Thursday, September 17, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. The meeting will be held at Gotham Center, 42-09 28th Street, room 14-43, in Long Island City, NY. The meeting will be also live-streamed and can be viewed on the NYC DOHMH YouTube channel: https://www.youtube.com/nychealth. Members of the public can attend the meeting at Gotham Center or virtually via the NYC DOHMH YouTube channel. Documents and/or records from the meeting will be posted on the NYC DOHMHs webpage at https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/about/hearings-and-notices/official-notices.page
watching.plain: The New York City Board of Health will meet Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. at Gotham Center in Long Island City, with the meeting also livestreamed on the Health Department's YouTube channel.
